security_problem: The repository's verification paths mutated the tree they were verifying. harness/check.sh ran `make fmt` (`go fmt ./...`) and scripts/pre-commit ran `go mod tidy`, both of which rewrite tracked files. cmd/visor-workflow records a workspace snapshot digest before each command and rejects a later mismatch, so a single unformatted tracked file made an otherwise green task unreachable at HARNESS_VERIFIED with target_snapshot_mismatch. CI had no formatting check either, so the drift merged green, and no local hook warned the author. A commit also records the index rather than the working tree, so a file staged while unformatted and reformatted afterwards would pass a working-tree-only check and still fail CI.
required_behavior: Formatting is checked, never applied, on every verification path, and each check's enumeration of what it examines is provably complete. scripts/check-gofmt checks every Go file in the tree: the list comes from git, is NUL-delimited, fails closed when the listing fails or is truncated, and gofmt runs in bounded batches with `--` so odd filenames stay data. scripts/check-staged-gofmt closes the one gap the working-tree pass leaves: it enumerates index/worktree differences (`git diff --name-only -z -- '*.go'`) rather than a --diff-filter list, so a rename, a copy or any other change type cannot be dropped from the check, and it skips non-regular index entries (mode 120000 gitlinks and symlinks) because a symlink named *.go is not Go source; a path whose index content equals the file on disk is already proven by the working-tree pass. scripts/pre-commit calls both arms and uses `go mod tidy -diff`, which reports without writing. The CI Lint job runs check-gofmt and the staged-blob matrix, so a non-zero exit fails the job. scripts/tests/check-staged-gofmt_test.sh is the committed regression matrix for the staged arm: modified, new, renamed, parse error, clean, unstaged-only, symlink, staged deletion and empty index. harness/invariants.md records the rule as H51, adjacent to H50.
failure_behavior: A non-gofmt-clean tree, a staged blob that differs from the working tree and is unformatted, an unparsable Go file, a failed or truncated listing, an empty listing, and a missing gofmt all fail closed with a message naming the cause. Nothing is reformatted or rewritten, so recorded evidence keeps binding to the tree it was recorded against. Non-regular index entries and staged deletions do not block a commit. `make fmt` and `go mod tidy` remain available to developers and are never called from a verification path.
non_goals: Reformatting any Go file in this change
Replacing golangci-lint or adding new linters
Changing Makefile targets or the developer `make fmt` / `go mod tidy` workflow
Pinning or asserting a specific Go or gofmt version in the scripts
Touching any proxy, policy, audit or workflow logic beyond the Lint job steps
